objective: Qualitative priorities1/2: unsuccessful HAE bidders and named buyer acquisition criteria; no new valuation calculations.
method: Reused existing deal-history register; verified specific original KalVista passages; five targeted web queries and selective primary-source reading. No agents or bulk scraping.

findings.buyer: Anonymous KalVista Parties B and D
findings.observed: Both withdrew on valuation grounds and indicated willingness to re-engage below mid20s/share if lead process failed. PartyB had submitted19/share February25.
findings.inference: Observed demand beyond winning buyer, but no proof their needs remain unfilled or they want PHVS.
findings.counterevidence: Initial Feb-Apr2024 outreach to18strategics produced no serious transaction interest/proposals in that initial round; later PartyA offer must not be conflated with initial outreach. Successful-deal selection cannot estimate base rate.

findings.observed: Approximately1.9bn equity acquisition, largest to date; emphasizes rare immunology, global commercialization, US expansion and2030revenue target. ClosedJune11percompletionrelease.
findings.inference: Direct validation of willingness to buy oral HAE; its need may now be filled. Not automatically another PHVS bidder.

findings.observed: Blueprint9.1bn upfront equity and up to9.5bn includingCVR; oral marketed Ayvakit plus oral pipeline. CEO emphasizes rare/immunology,differentiatedmedicines,returns; says early-stage remains main interest and sizeable further acquisition capacity at that date.
findings.inference: Demonstrated adjacent asset appetite, stronger than generic rare-disease statement. Mast-cell biology is not bradykinin HAE. Capacity statement historical, not verified current dry powder; no PHVS contact.

findings.observed: BD leadership cites Shire acquisition, oralTYK2Nimbus acquisition and late-stage licensing transactions.
findings.inference: Proven use of acquisitions and licenses; combined with existing HAE franchise gives plausible fit. No explicit PHVS interest or HAE acquisition mandate.

findings.observed: Explicit commitment to expand HAE portfolio/full range of patients, with current focus on expanding homegrownAndembry.
findings.inference: Disease commitment, not oral acquisition mandate; own launch provides competing capital priority and product overlap.

decision: Material strategic optionality and demonstrated sector demand, not evidence of high PHVS takeover probability within a specified horizon. No numeric probability change. Failed bidders anonymous; do not identify them from weak clues.
model_architecture_only: Acquisition replaces standalone outcome at defined horizon rather than adding full purchase price to standalone value.
Retain necessary development,manufacturing,medical affairs and commercial costs; remove only avoidable/duplicate costs.
Buyer value not equal shareholder consideration; bargaining shares synergies.
Acquisition probability and price should depend on clinical/commercial outcomes rather than be an independent upside draw.
stop_rule: Bounded pass complete; further probability upgrade requires PHVS-specific interest/process evidence or a better-defined empirical base rate, not more generic fit.
